title: Indian Photographers Lose ₹40 Lakh Camera Gear in Italy, Police Refuse Help on Sunday
excerpt: Two photographers had professional equipment worth approximately $50,000 stolen during an Italy trip, but local police declined to register a complaint because it was a Sunday.
body:
• Two Indian photographers had camera equipment worth ₹40-44 lakh (approximately $50,000) stolen while traveling in Italy.
  • Italian police allegedly refused to register a complaint or help because the theft was reported on a Sunday.
  • Some of the stolen items had tracking devices, but the photographers were unable to recover them without police assistance.
  • The incident highlights growing concerns about petty theft targeting tourists in popular European destinations.

Two Indian photographers have alleged that camera gear worth ₹40-44 lakh (approximately $50,000) was stolen during a trip to Italy, with local police refusing to file a report or offer assistance because the theft occurred on a Sunday, according to Moneycontrol and News18.

The photographers described the experience as "most frustrating," with the refusal of Italian law enforcement to engage on a non-working day leaving them without the official documentation needed to pursue insurance claims or track the stolen equipment.

Tracking Devices Proved Futile

In a particularly galling detail, some of the stolen camera equipment had tracking devices attached, meaning the photographers could potentially locate their gear electronically. However, without police cooperation, they were unable to act on the tracking data or enlist local authorities to help recover the items, according to Inshorts.

The total value of the stolen equipment — including cameras, lenses, and professional photography accessories — was estimated at between ₹40 lakh and ₹44 lakh across multiple reports, a significant loss for working photographers whose livelihoods depend on their gear.

A Pattern of Tourist Theft in Italy

The incident underscores a well-documented pattern of theft targeting tourists, particularly those carrying expensive camera equipment, across Italy's major cities and transit routes. Italy's train networks, tourist hotspots, and crowded urban areas have long been known as hunting grounds for professional pickpockets and organized theft rings.

In November 2025, Swedish photographer Roger Radstrom had his entire camera bag — worth roughly $8,000 — stolen from under his table at a restaurant in Milan, according to PetaPixel. Like the Indian photographers, he reported unhelpful police who "seem to dislike their work."

In 2024, American YouTuber and former police officer Manny Ortiz lost $16,000 worth of camera gear on a train from Rome to Venice. He described the theft as a coordinated operation involving multiple individuals, a pattern that investigators say is common on Italian rail networks.

Travel Advisory for Indian Tourists

The incident has resonated widely with India's growing community of international travelers and content creators. Italy is among the most popular European destinations for Indian tourists, with visitor numbers rising steadily in recent years.

Travel experts recommend several precautions for photographers traveling in Europe: carrying equipment in nondescript bags rather than branded camera cases, using tracking devices such as Apple AirTags, purchasing comprehensive travel insurance that covers equipment theft, and never leaving bags unattended even briefly in public spaces.

For Indian citizens who are victims of theft abroad, the Indian embassy or nearest consulate can provide assistance with filing local police reports and coordinating with authorities, even when local law enforcement is uncooperative.

What's Next

The photographers' experience has gone viral on Indian social media, with many users sharing their own stories of theft and police indifference while traveling in Europe. Whether the photographers will be able to recover their equipment through tracking data or insurance claims remains unclear. The incident adds to a growing body of cautionary tales for Indian travelers heading to popular European destinations.
nri_angle: The incident highlights travel safety concerns for Indian tourists and professionals traveling abroad, particularly in popular European destinations.
